title: の — possession (“’s / of”) and ‘the one that ～’
summary: の links two nouns, as in ‘B of A’ or ‘A’s B’. It can also stand in for a noun that has already been mentioned, giving ‘the ～ one’. Noun + の + noun; adjective (い) + の for ‘the ～ one’.

patterns.gloss: B belonging to A (先生の本 = the teacher's book)
stands in for a noun: ‘the ～ one’ (赤いの = the red one)

body.p: A の B shows that B belongs to or is related to A: 先生の本 (the teacher's book), 母のかばん (my mother's bag). The order is the reverse of English ‘of’: owner first, thing second.
When the noun is clear from context, you can drop it and let の stand in: 赤いのがほしいです (I want the red one). This works after い-adjectives and nouns.
の after a verb turns it into a noun phrase (歌うのが好き, ‘like singing’). You will see this in later grammar points.

examples.ja: これは先生（せんせい）の本（ほん）です。
examples.romaji: Kore wa sensei no hon desu.

examples.ja: これは母（はは）のかばんです。
examples.romaji: Kore wa haha no kaban desu.
examples.note: 母 is used for your own mother when speaking to others.

examples.ja: 赤（あか）いのがほしいです。
examples.note: 赤いの = 赤いもの; の replaces the noun.

pitfalls: Keep the order: owner の thing. 先生の本 is the teacher's book, not 本の先生.
To mean ‘the ～ one’, a な-adjective needs な + の (きれいなの), not just の.
